transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How can I help you today?

Hi, Dr. Smith, I'm Alice. I decided to come in because I keep getting stuck on these ideas that people around me are plotting or judging me, even when they swear they aren’t. It's just really hard to shake the feeling that everyone is working against me.
Have these suspicious thoughts ever led you to believe that people are spying on you, sending you hidden messages, or conspiring against you in an organized way?

Yes, I've felt like there is an organized plan behind my back to make me fail. For instance, when my supervisor moved me off a big EV job, I became convinced he and my husband had secretly teamed up and decided I couldn't be trusted. Even though they both deny it, I just can't shake the feeling that they are working together against me.
Have you ever heard voices or experienced any strange sensations that others don't seem to notice, especially when no one is around?

Yes, I have. Sometimes, especially when I'm alone late at night in the garage or at home, I hear a man's voice commenting on what I'm doing. He'll say things like "They're laughing at you" or "You're wasting your time," even though I know there's nobody actually there.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F22", "F20"], but based on this conversation, F22 (Delusional Disorder) is less likely because the patient reports auditory hallucinations (hearing a man's voice commenting when alone), which are not typical in F22 where hallucinations are absent or not prominent. The presence of both persistent delusions (organized plot against her) and auditory hallucinations, especially with themes of persecution and self-reference, strongly supports a diagnosis within the schizophrenia spectrum. Therefore, F20 (Schizophrenia) is now the primary candidate.

Symptoms have been persistent and are causing significant distress, meeting criteria for paranoid schizophrenia.
